title: Ticketifier: convert Sales/CS enterprise asks into prioritized, scorable tickets
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success submit high-touch enterprise feature asks as freeform notes, email threads, or ad-hoc docs. That creates friction: inconsistent scoping, duplicate requests, long time-to-decision, and poor prioritization alignment with platform constraints (Dedicated vs Private).

Goal: Build a lightweight 'Ticketifier' process and artifact set that turns an incoming enterprise ask into a structured, scoreable Linear ticket plus a short scoping brief. The output must be consistent enough for rapid PM triage, clear enough for Solutions Eng / Design to estimate, and flexible enough to handle compliance-driven requests.

Scope: 1) Intake schema (form + Slack bot + GitHub/GTM email template) with required fields: problem statement, affected customer(s) and ARR tier, desired behavior, data sensitivity, suggested SLA/region needs, compliance/regulatory notes, and indicative success metrics. 2) A 5-factor scoring rubric (Customer Value, Strategic Alignment, Technical Feasibility, Operational Cost, Compliance Risk) with recommended weightings and examples. 3) A default PRD-lite template auto-attached to created tickets and a one-pager generator for customer-facing scoping. 4) Small automation to map high-score tickets into a 'fast-track' review pipeline and flag Dedicated/Private implications for infra. 5) Pilot and feedback loop with two AE/CS pods and one strategic account manager for 4 weeks.

Non-goals: Full engineering estimates and long-form PRDs are out of scope for this ticket — aim is to generate a consistent, triage-ready artifact and routing decision.

Why this matters: Improves time-to-first-decision, reduces repeated clarifying cycles between Sales/CS and PM, creates a consistent audit trail for enterprise asks, and surfaces Dedicated/Private signals earlier to infra and security teams.
acceptance_criteria: Intake schema drafted and hosted as a Google Form + Slack slash-command to create a draft ticket
Scoring rubric document published in Confluence with examples for low/medium/high in each factor
Linear ticket template auto-populates title, customer, and first-pass score when intake is used
Pilot run completed with 12 incoming asks from Sales/CS and a post-pilot feedback survey with >=75% satisfaction from pilot POCs
Routing rules created to flag tickets that likely require Dedicated or Private deployment and notify ENG-Infra and Security channels
comments: 2026-03-04 - Aisha K: Kickoff with Solutions Eng and Growth ops. Agreed to keep the initial form to <= 12 fields to maximize completion rates.

2026-03-06 - Liam C: Prototype intake form posted in #sales-cs-intake for comment. Rachel from AE asked for an optional field to upload customer-side architecture diagrams; agreed to add as optional attachment link.
2026-03-08 - Miro note: Design (DES-204) will supply 1 slide for the one-pager generator layout; aim to keep the one-pager < 400 words.
2026-03-09 - Eng (ENG-99012) flagged that Private deployment requests must include KMS/HSM needs; added as a mandatory checkbox in the schema when 'Private' is selected.

2026-03-11 - PM review: Weighting proposal for rubric moved from equal weights to customer-value-heavy (40%), feasibility (25%), ops cost (15%), strategic fit (10%), compliance risk (-10 to -30 penalty). Need legal sign-off on compliance penalty approach.

2026-03-12 - Feedback from pilot AE: worries about duplicate requests. Action: add quick duplicate-check prompt that searches for keywords in recent 6 months of Linear tickets and surfaces possible matches in the intake confirmation message.
2026-03-14 - Liam C: Draft Confluence page ready at https://confluence.redwood.ai/enterprise/ticketifier-draft; shared with Growth and Infra for comment. Pilot start scheduled 2026-03-16.
